haiku-low.q1: Captured amount minus the sum of amount_cents of pending and succeeded refunds on the payment. Failed refunds do not count.
haiku-low.q2: It retries up to 3 more times (4 attempts total) with the same idempotency key, a 10-second timeout each. If all fail, the refund stays pending.
haiku-low.q3: No retry. The refund is marked failed only if still pending, the provider's message is stored and shown, and the amount is freed.
haiku-low.q4: The refund reaching succeeded status, via the shared transition from a webhook, the immediate provider reply, or the sweeper. That inserts one outbox row, sent once.
haiku-low.q5: Only succeeded refunds decide it: sum equals captured amount means Refunded, above zero but less means Partially refunded. It changes in the same transaction a refund succeeds.
haiku-low.q6: A SELECT ... FOR UPDATE row lock on the payment serializes the admins. The second rechecks captured status and the pending plus succeeded sum, and is rejected if over.
haiku-low.q7: Our server generates a UUID at reservation in step 3 and stores it on the refund row as idempotency_key. Every retry and sweeper call reuses that saved key.
haiku-low.q8: Unique provider_event_id makes duplicate events return 200 without reprocessing. The transition's conditional update changes only pending rows. Email outbox row is unique per refund.
haiku-low.q9: It stays pending with no provider_refund_id, because the provider may have created the refund. Marking it failed could be wrong. The sweeper retries with the same key.
haiku-low.q10: The sweeper runs every 15 minutes on refunds unchecked for 6 hours. Final status goes to the transition, pending updates last_checked_at, and errors stay pending with alerts.
haiku-low.q11: It shows the refund as pending, awaiting provider confirmation, or failed with the provider's message, or an error. The order status does not change.

sonnet.q1: refundable = captured amount minus the sum of amount_cents of pending and succeeded refunds on that payment (failed refunds don't count).
sonnet.q2: Retried with the same idempotency key, up to 3 retries (4 attempts total), short backoff, 10-second timeout each; each failed attempt gets an audit row and the refund stays pending. After the last retry it is left pending with no provider_refund_id (not marked failed) and the sweeper keeps trying.
sonnet.q3: No retry. In one transaction, status is set to failed (only if still pending), the provider's message goes in provider_error, resolved_at is set, and an audit row is written. The admin sees the provider's message, and the amount becomes available again because failed refunds don't count.
sonnet.q4: The refund reaching succeeded: step 8 inserts an email_outbox row in the same transaction, and a worker then sends the email. Failed refunds get no outbox row and no email.
sonnet.q5: The sum of amount_cents of the payment's succeeded refunds: equal to the captured amount means Refunded; above 0 but less means Partially refunded. Pending and failed refunds are ignored. It changes only when a refund becomes succeeded, inside the same transaction as that status change.
sonnet.q6: In the reservation transaction the server locks the payment row with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, so the two requests run one after the other. It re-checks captured status, sums pending+succeeded refunds, and rolls back with 'exceeds refundable amount (X cents left)' if the sum plus the new amount exceeds the captured amount. Otherwise it inserts a pending refund (reserving the amount) and commits.
sonnet.q7: Our server generates the UUID idempotency key when it creates the refund row in step 3. It is stored in refunds.idempotency_key (unique), committed before any provider call, and every later retry (step 5 and the sweeper) reuses the stored key.
sonnet.q8: Status: webhook events are inserted into refund_webhook_events with a unique provider_event_id (duplicate returns 200 and stops), and the shared transition runs UPDATE ... WHERE status='pending', so if no row changes nothing more happens; contradictory events get a 'conflicting event ignored' audit row and an alert. Email: email_outbox.refund_id is unique, so at most one row per refund even if success is processed twice. A rare duplicate send after a worker crash is still possible, reduced by the email service's idempotency key (whether it supports one is not known).
sonnet.q9: Pending, with no provider_refund_id. It is not marked failed because the provider may have actually created the refund (a timed-out call may have succeeded). The sweeper keeps trying with the same key, and the admin sees 'submitted, awaiting provider confirmation'.
sonnet.q10: The sweeper, a scheduled job running every 15 minutes. It selects pending refunds with last_checked_at null or older than 6 hours, or with null provider_refund_id and no recent attempt. With a provider_refund_id it fetches the current status. Without one and under 24 hours old it repeats the create call with the stored idempotency key. Without one and over 24 hours old it looks up by charge id and our refund id metadata, never creating a new one; if the provider has no match it marks the refund failed with an audit note and alert, and if the lookup fails it stays pending and alerts. A final status goes to the shared transition with actor system:sweeper. If still pending, it updates only last_checked_at and writes an audit row. On provider error the refund stays pending and the next run retries. An alert fires if any pending refund is over 20 hours old without a successful check.
sonnet.q11: The refund as pending (e.g. 'submitted, awaiting provider confirmation' when there is no provider confirmation yet, or pending after acceptance), or the provider's message if it was rejected (4xx), or an error. The order status does not change, and the refund appears in the payment's refund list.
